title: Boosting E-commerce Content Diversity: A Graph-based RAG Approach with User Reviews

problem.claim: Automated e-commerce content generation must produce product copy efficiently while capturing nuanced item details and maintaining diversity.

gap.claim: Existing LLM-based approaches lack diversity and do not fully capture nuanced details of specific items.

contributions.claim: A framework integrates graph-based knowledge into Retrieval-Augmented Generation for e-commerce content generation.
User reviews are used to construct an item-feature graph containing explicit and implicit item-feature connections.
A graph traversal mechanism explores a broader range of item-related features to provide varied and informative generation inputs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments showing significantly improved diversity while preserving fidelity.

narrative_sequence.summary: E-commerce product copy influences purchasing decisions, while manual creation is costly and time-consuming at catalog scale.
LLMs offer automation potential but remain limited by insufficient diversity and incomplete understanding of item-specific details.
The proposed framework combines graph-based knowledge with RAG, using user reviews to build an item-feature graph and traversing it for broader feature retrieval.
The authors report improved diversity with preserved fidelity in extensive experiments.

source_observation.claim: The approach uses structured connections between items and features to retrieve diverse, contextually relevant, and factually grounded information.

interpretation.claim: Representing domain relationships explicitly may help generation systems balance diversity with item-specific grounding.

application.claim: For domain content generation, construct a relationship graph from user-generated or domain-specific evidence and use graph traversal to broaden retrieval.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond e-commerce content generation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not detail the graph construction procedure or traversal algorithm.
The abstract does not report computational costs, failure cases, or human evaluation.
